version.promotional_text: A hand-drawn penguin checks the forecast and dresses for it. Sweater, raincoat or bikini: one look and you know what to wear.
version.description:
Weather Penguin tells you what to wear today, at a glance.

Open the app and a hand-drawn penguin is already dressed for the weather where you are: a sweater and scarf when it's cold, a jacket when it's cool, a T-shirt when it's warm and a bikini when it's hot. When rain is on the way, out come the raincoat, the poncho or the swim cap.

• Today and tomorrow: swipe to see what the penguin will wear tomorrow
• Your temperatures: choose when the penguin switches from sweater to jacket to T-shirt
• Morning penguin: an optional notification each morning with what to wear
• Widgets for your Home Screen and Lock Screen
• Ask Siri what to wear
• An Apple Watch app and watch face complications
• °F or °C
• iMessage stickers of every outfit
• Your settings follow you to your other devices with iCloud
• No account, no ads, no tracking

Weather data from Apple Weather.

review_notes:
Weather Penguin shows a hand-drawn penguin dressed for the weather where the user is, today and tomorrow. No account, no login, no in-app purchases, no ads, no user-generated content, no chat. A video of the app in use is attached (sample weather, on simulators).

PURPOSE AND AUDIENCE
For anyone deciding what to wear when they go out, children included: one look at the penguin answers "what should I wear today?" without reading a forecast. Weather Penguin has been on the App Store since 2013 (version 1.3); 2.0 is a rebuild with the same drawings, the same rules and the same settings.

HOW TO USE IT (no setup needed)
- Launch the app and allow location (While Using the App). The penguin for today appears, with the temperature, the high or low, the condition and, when rain is coming, a raincoat and falling rain.
- Swipe left for tomorrow. On iPad and in landscape, today and tomorrow are side by side.
- The gear (top right) opens Settings: one slider with three handles sets the temperatures where the penguin changes into a jacket, a T-shirt and a bikini; F or C; and Morning penguin, off by default (a local notification at a time the user picks, with what to wear and the day's drawing).
- If location is declined, the app says so and has a button that opens its page in the Settings app.
- Widgets: Home Screen (small and medium) and Lock Screen (circular, rectangular, inline). Each asks for location once.
- Siri and Shortcuts: "What should I wear in Weather Penguin" answers with the advice and shows the penguin.
- Apple Watch: today and tomorrow (turn the Digital Crown), and watch face complications.
- iMessage: a sticker pack of the eight penguins.

WHAT THE APP ADDS ON iOS
The main screen is drawn with HTML bundled inside the app; no website is loaded and nothing depends on our servers. Around it the app is native: location, the forecast from Apple WeatherKit, Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, the Apple Watch app and complications, a Siri and Shortcuts action (App Intents), local notifications with a picture, iCloud sync of settings between the user's devices, Dynamic Type, and layouts for iPad, Split View and iPhone Duo. weatherpenguin.com has only a demo with sample weather.

EXTERNAL SERVICES
Apple WeatherKit for the forecast (the Apple Weather mark is on the main screen and links to Apple's data sources page; Settings shows it too), Apple's geocoder for the city name, and iCloud key-value storage for settings. Anonymous usage counts go to GoatCounter: no personal data, no identifiers, no location, no cookies. Not tracking (App Privacy: Coarse Location and Product Interaction, not linked to the user).

REGIONS
Works wherever Apple Weather has forecasts, in 17 languages that follow the device's language; F or C follows the device's setting.

REGULATION AND THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL
Not a regulated industry and not a medical or safety app. Weather data: Apple Weather. The penguin drawings and the icon are original, hand-drawn for the app. Font: Inter (SIL Open Font License).
